benchmark_text: People are alike in many ways and different in many ways.
connections_to_other_maps: COPING WITH MENTAL DISTRESS; HEREDITY AND EXPERIENCE SHAPE BEHAVIOR

benchmark_text: Different families or schools have different rules and patterns for behavior. Some behaviors are not accepted in most families or schools.
People often choose to dress talk and act like their friends. They also often choose to do certain things in their own way.
People can learn about others from direct experience from the mass communications media and from listening to other people talk about their work and their lives.
Sometimes people feel uncomfortable with people who dress talk or act very differently from them.
Different cultures have different patterns of behavior that are exhibited by people who grow up in those cultures.
Within a large society there are a variety of groups whose identities are determined in part by the social class gender ethnicity or the region of the country where they live.

Although within any society there is usually broad general agreement on what behavior is unacceptable the standards used to judge behavior vary for different settings and subgroups and they may change with time and different political and economic conditions.
Rewards and punishments vary widely among and even within different societies.
Technology especially in transportation and communication is increasingly important in spreading ideas values and behavior patterns within a society and among different societies.
connections_to_other_maps: COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY; INTERACTION OF TECHNOLOGY AND SOCIETY; INFLUENCES ON SOCIAL CHANGE

benchmark_text: What is considered to be acceptable behavior varies from culture to culture and from one time period to another but there are some behaviors that are unacceptable in almost all cultures past and present.

Cultural beliefs strongly influence the values and behavior of the people who grow up in the culture often without their being fully aware of it. Responses to these influences varies among individuals.
The ways that unacceptable social behavior is punished depend partly on beliefs about the purposes of punishment and about its effectiveness.
Social distinctions are a part of every culture but take many different forms ranging from rigid classes based solely on parentage to gradations based on the acquisition of skill wealth or education.
Differences in the behavior of individuals arise from the interaction of heredity culture and experience—the effect of each depends on the other.
People are born into some groups placed into some groups and choose to join some groups.
The way people act is often influenced by the groups to which they belong.

Different groups have different expectations for how their members should act. Sometimes rules are written down and strictly enforced and sometimes the expectations are understood by observing how others behave.
When acting together members of a group and even people in a crowd sometimes do and say things good or bad that they would not do or say on their own.
People join groups because they like to do certain things and they like to be with others who do those things.

Being a member of a group often has personal advantages such as companionship a sense of identity and recognition by others inside and outside the group. Group identity may also create a sense of separation from other groups or individuals.

People sometimes react to all members of a group as though they were the same and perceive in the members behavior only those qualities that fit preconceptions of the group. Such stereotyping leads to uncritical judgments.
Some groups result from the creation of an organization. Others exist only in the sense that members share some common characteristics or interests.
Organizations usually have explicitly stated social business or political purposes but they also often have purposes beyond those for which they officially exist.
When individuals act together as a group it can be difficult to assign blame or credit to any one person.
Changes happen in everyones life sometimes suddenly more often slowly. People cannot control some changes but they can usually learn to cope with them.

benchmark_text: Although rules at home school church and in the community stay mostly the same sometimes they change. Changes in social arrangements happen because some rules do not work new people are involved or outside circumstances change.
Rules can sometimes be changed by getting whoever made the rules to agree to change them.

Some aspects of family and community life are the same now as a generation ago but some aspects are very different. What is taught in school and school policies have been changed over the years in response to family and community pressures.
By the way they depict the ideas and customs of one culture communications media may stimulate changes in other cultures.
Migration conquest and natural disasters have been major factors in causing social and cultural change.
The size and rate of growth of the human population in any location are affected by economic political religious technological and environmental factors.
The decisions of one generation both provide and limit the range of the possibilities open to the next generation.
Mass media migration and conquest affect social change by exposing one culture to another.
To various degrees governments try to bring about social change or impede it through policies laws incentives or direct coercion.
Getting something one wants may mean giving up something in return.

benchmark_text: Different people may make different choices for different reasons.
Choices have consequences some more serious than others.
In making decisions it helps to take time to consider the benefits and drawbacks of alternatives.
In making decisions benefits and drawbacks of alternatives can be taken into account more effectively if the people who will be affected are involved.
Sometimes social decisions have unexpected consequences no matter how carefully the decisions are made.
There are trade-offs that each person must consider in making choices—about personal popularity health family relations and education for example—that often have lifelong consequences.
connections_to_other_maps: AVOIDING BIAS IN SCIENCE; HEREDITY AND EXPERIENCE SHAPE BEHAVIOR

benchmark_text: One common aspect of all social trade-offs pits personal benefit and rights of the individual on one side against the general social good on the other.
Trade-offs are not always between desirable possibilities. Sometimes social and personal trade-offs require accepting an unwanted outcome to avoid some other unwanted one.
Benefits and costs of proposed choices include consequences that are long-term as well as short-term and indirect as well as direct.
connections_to_other_maps: DECISIONS ABOUT USING TECHNOLOGY; STATISTICAL REASONING

benchmark_text: In deciding among alternatives a major question is who will receive the benefits and who (not necessarily the same people) will bear the costs.
Social trade-offs are often generational. The cost of benefits received by one generation may fall on subsequent generations.
It is difficult to compare potential benefits of social alternatives. One reason is that there is no common measure for different forms of good.
Peaceful efforts at social change are most successful when the affected people are included in the planning.
Rules can help to make sure that everyone is treated fairly.
People often trade things they have for things that they want.
People who live together in a group often reach an agreement about what each will contribute to the others in the group.
Sometimes a community decides to make certain services—such as schools libraries parks mail service and police and fire protection—equally available to all its members through government agencies.
People often compete for resources when their supply is limited.
Trading things people have or things they want for money is often more convenient than trading those things directly.
The value of something depends on how much of it is available and how many people want it.
In some groups decisions are made by and disputes settled by recognized authorities such as parents teachers bosses or elected officials.

Government provides some goods and services through its own agencies and some through contracts with private individuals or businesses. To pay for the goods and services government must obtain money by taxing people or by borrowing the money.
Governments are run by people who come into power by election appointment or force.
Governments usually have most of the power to make revise interpret and enforce the rules and decisions that determine how a community state or nation is run.

benchmark_text: Some industries are controlled by government agencies that decide which goods or services to provide and how to distribute them based on various political considerations.

Some industries are privately owned and controlled by many different individuals or groups of individuals that decide which goods or services to provide based on what they believe will personally benefit them the most.
Almost all societies have some industries that are privately owned and some that are run by government agencies.
The goods and services that people want are supplied by individuals or by groups of individuals.
The political system of a nation is closely intertwined with its economic system refereeing the economic activity of individuals and groups at every level.
In a free-market economic system it is assumed that free competition produces the best allocation of resources the greatest productivity and the lowest costs.
In almost all societies governments run some industries for the benefit of the society as a whole.

Governments can use a variety of strategies to keep a free-market system functioning efficiently and to protect individuals and the society as a whole from the negative effects of free-market behavior.
Disagreements may occur between family members friends and others.
Some ways of dealing with disagreements work better than others. People who are not involved in a dispute may be helpful in solving it.
Rules at home at school and in the community let people know how to behave and what to expect from others and so can reduce the number of disputes.
Communicating the different points of view in a dispute is a first step in finding a satisfactory compromise.
Resolving a conflict by force rather than compromise can lead to more problems.
One persons exercise of freedom may conflict with the freedom of others. Rules can help to resolve conflicting freedoms.

benchmark_text: If a conflict cannot be settled by compromise it may be decided by a vote—if everyone agrees to accept the results.

Groups are sometimes formed to consolidate influence or power through pooled resources and concerted action. The formation of a group highlights the differences between people who are members and those who are not and may lead to conflict between them.
Most groups have formal or informal procedures for arbitrating conflicts between their members.
Conflict between people or groups arises from competition over ideas resources power and status.
Social change or the prospect of it often promotes conflict.
Social change or the prospect of it promotes conflict because social economic and political changes usually benefit some groups more than others.
Conflicts are difficult to resolve when there are few choices or there is little room for compromise.
The use of pamphlets demonstrations cartoons etc. may provide an outlet for people to voice their frustrations without resorting to violence.
Conflict between people or groups is sometimes reduced when the groups in conflict are fighting a common adversary.
Conflict does not necessarily end when one side gets a decision in its favor for the losers may then work all the harder to reverse modify or circumvent the decision.
Conflicts can be resolved through direct negotiation and compromise by the people or groups involved or through an appeal to an outside authority such as a court.
Many of the things people eat and wear come from other countries.
Trade occurs between individual people between nations and between regions in the same nation.
For many things they need people rely on others who are not part of their family and may not even be part of their local community.
Trade between nations occurs when natural resources or the skill to make something are unevenly distributed or when the costs of production are very different in different countries.

The economic well-being of a country may be enhanced by improving the skill and motivation of its workforce by developing equipment or practices that are more efficient and produce higher quality products and services and by engaging in trade with other nations.
Treaties are negotiated between two or more nations to establish or maintain peaceful relationships to define parameters for trade or to create political or military alliances.
The global environment is affected by national and international policies and practices relating to energy use waste disposal ecological management manufacturing and population.
Communication and transportation technologies influence how much people in different countries may interact whether it be for political economic or social purposes.

International organizations such as the United Nations the World Bank and the European Union provide a structure for nations to communicate reach consensus and negotiate treaties but these organizations often have only limited authority over their members.
Treaties do not affect all of the people in a country equally.
The wealth of a country depends on the balance between how much its resources and products are sought by other nations and how much of other nations resources and products it seeks.
International trade is often complicated by political motivations taking priority over economic ones.
The migration of workers between nations—temporary and permanent legal and illegal—plays a major role in the quality and availability of the workforce in many nations.
The growing worldwide interdependence of social economic and ecological systems means that changes in one place in the world may have effects in any other place.

Communication and transportation technologies coupled with political and economic policies now allow people to interact with people in different countries almost as easily as they interact with people in their own country.
